events.message: We are taking the useful things with us. Earlier creations remain where we made them.
Leavened dough. Yeast changes the dough over time; the game compresses fermentation.
Yogurt. A suitable bacterial culture transforms milk; it is not the same culture as bread yeast.
We are taking the useful things with us. Earlier creations remain where we made them.
Humoral menu. A period menu organized through hot/cold and wet/dry qualities. This records a historical belief, not a medically effective diet.
Annotated menu. A museum annotation distinguishes a historical explanatory system from present-day nutrition; neither is a literal ingredient.

playerReport: Stopped voluntarily at pastry workshop, not blocked. The roadside meal was clear and mildly satisfying. The two cultures made sense, but dough plus yeast failed twice until I learned to place both in the fermentation room; the generic failure did not explain that distinction. Once learned, yogurt was routine placement then combination. I tried fruit yogurt and buttered bread for pleasure and neither worked, which reduced my urge to experiment. The humoral menu side branch was a welcome oddity, reached with a hint, then annotated successfully. Returning to flour plus butter failed; I suspect the cool bench is required, but another place-both-and-combine sequence no longer interested me enough to continue. I did not reach the ending. This is a logical-interface impression only.
